_note: Draft English of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Bereshit 26 (Isaac/Abimelech, wells, blessing). Saadia-specific moves: v.8 'ילאעב' = 'jesting/playing' (Saadia mutes the sexual implication of מצחק); v.20-21 'שגלא' / 'ד'את אלענאד' = 'Strife' / 'Obstinate One' (Saadia translates the well-names by their meaning); v.22 'ד'את אלסעה' = 'the spacious one' for רחבות.

translations.1: Then there was a famine in the land — apart from the first famine which had been in Abraham's time — and Isaac went to Abimelech, king of the Philistines, to al-Khalus (Gerar).
translations.2: And God appeared to him, and said: 'Do not go down to Egypt; dwell in the land which I shall tell you.
translations.3: Without delay, settle in this land, and I shall be with you, and bless you; for to you and to your offspring I shall give all these lands; and I shall fulfill the oath which I swore to Abraham your father.
translations.4: And I shall multiply your offspring like the stars of the sky; and I shall give them all these lands; and in them shall all the nations of the earth be blessed —
translations.5: in recompense for that Abraham accepted My command, and kept what I charged him with — of My charges, My statutes, and My laws.'
translations.7: And when the men of the place asked him about his wife, he said: 'She is my sister' — for he was afraid to say, 'She is my wife,' saying within himself: 'Lest the men of the place kill me on her account, for she is beautiful in appearance.'
translations.8: And when the days of his stay grew long there, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out from a window of his, and saw — and behold, Isaac was jesting with Rebekah his wife.
translations.10: And he said to him: 'What is this you have done to us? Soon, had one of our people lain with her, you would have brought guilt upon us.'
translations.11: And Abimelech proclaimed to all his people, and said: 'Whoever harms this man or his wife shall surely be put to death.'
translations.12: Then Isaac sowed in that land; and he found in that year a hundredfold, by estimate; and God blessed him.
translations.13: And the man grew great, and continued — each time time passed, he grew greater — until he was exceedingly great.
translations.14: And he had flocks of sheep and herds of cattle, and a great household; until the Philistines envied him.
translations.15: And all the wells which his father Abraham's servants had dug in his time — the Philistines had stopped them up, and filled them with dust.
translations.16: And Abimelech said to Isaac: 'Go from us — for you have grown mightier than we, exceedingly.'
translations.17: So Isaac went from there, and encamped in the valley of al-Khalus (Gerar), and settled there.
translations.18: And Isaac returned, and dug the wells which had been dug in the time of Abraham his father — which the Philistines had stopped after his death — and he named them by names, as his father had named them.
translations.19: And when Isaac's servants dug in the valley, they found there a well of flowing water.
translations.20: And the herdsmen of al-Khalus (Gerar) quarreled with Isaac's herdsmen, saying: 'The water is ours.' And he named it Strife — for they had quarreled with him.
translations.21: And they dug another well, and they quarreled also over it; and he named it Obstinacy.
translations.22: Then he moved on from there, and dug another well; and they did not quarrel over it. And he named it Spaciousness — for he said: 'Now God has made spacious for us, and shall make us grow in the land.'
translations.23: Then he went up from there to Beer-Sheba.
translations.24: And God appeared to him in that night, and said: 'I am the God of Abraham your father; fear not, for I am with you; I shall bless you, and multiply your offspring, on account of Abraham My servant.'
translations.25: And he built there an altar, and called upon the name of God; and he pitched his tent there; and Isaac's servants dug there a well.
translations.26: And Abimelech went to him from al-Khalus (Gerar) — and Ahuzzath his companion, and Phicol the chief of his army.
translations.27: And Isaac said to them: 'Why have you come to me? You have hated me, and sent me away from you.'
translations.28: They said: 'We have indeed seen that God is with you, and we said, "Let there be an oath between us and you, and let us make a covenant with you:
translations.29: that you shall not do us evil, as we have not harmed you, and as we have done with you only good, and have sent you away in peace; you are now the blessed of God."'
translations.30: And he made them a feast; and they ate and drank there.
translations.31: And they rose early in the morning, and each man swore to his brother. And Isaac sent them away, and they went from him in peace.
translations.32: And it was on that day that Isaac's servants came, and told him concerning the well that they had dug, and said to him: 'We have found water.'
translations.33: And he called it Shibah; therefore the name of the town is Beer-Sheba to this day.
translations.34: And when Esau was a son of forty years, he took as a wife a woman whose name was Judith, daughter of Beeri the Hittite — and Basemath, daughter of Elon the Hittite.
translations.35: And they were a vexation of spirit to Isaac and Rebekah.
